examples.note: Pregame Starting XI graphic is highly readable; no major failure moment observed.
Venue line 'Emirates Stadium' in match intro is smaller than team names, so secondary text can be missed on small screens.

assets.issues: Strong in pregame graphics, but 'Emirates Stadium' functions as secondary text rather than dominant sponsor copy, so brand recall is weaker than a dedicated slate.
assets.suggestions: If venue naming rights are meant to work as paid exposure, isolate 'Emirates' in a larger font or contrasting panel instead of embedding it as part of venue text.

examples.note: On Aubameyang close-up the shirt-front is clear, but folds in the shirt slightly distort the wordmark.
During the front-flip celebration the logo is visible but motion blur reduces perfect readability.

assets.issues: Very strong white-on-red contrast, but legibility drops during celebrations and running shots because of torso rotation and fabric creasing.
assets.suggestions: Best-in-class contrast already; gains would come from securing more close-up chest-level shots in celebrations and replays rather than creative changes.

examples.note: Seen as secondary background signage during manager handshake; not isolated long enough for full sponsor impact.

assets.issues: Readable as fascia/tunnel branding but not held in frame long enough to deliver premium sponsorship value.
assets.suggestions: Use repeated larger-format tunnel/fascia panels with more negative space around the wordmark so short cutaways still read instantly.

brands.name: Emirates
brands.summary: Highest-value exposure comes from Arsenal shirt-front plus pregame/venue-related signage. Strong brand recall, with the main weakness being motion blur during celebrations and the sponsor sometimes appearing as venue text rather than standalone branding.

examples.note: Jan Vertonghen close-up is clear, but head-down posture slightly compresses the chest mark.
Son walk-off shot is readable, though partial body framing briefly crops the lower part of the shirt.
Lucas Moura entry shot is brief; logo is visible but exposure duration is short.

assets.issues: Excellent red-on-white contrast and strong central chest placement. Main limitation is brief duration in close-ups and occasional cropping during substitution coverage.
assets.suggestions: No creative fix needed; maximize value by favoring tighter isolated player close-ups during stoppages and substitutions where the chest mark is square to camera.

brands.name: AIA
brands.summary: Very strong shirt-front sponsor: bold, central, and highly legible in stoppages and player close-ups. Exposure quality is better in substitutions/stoppages than in open play.

examples.note: Visible on Tottenham kit near kickoff, but very small in the wide opening shot.
Seen in substitution close-ups, but the swoosh is tiny relative to frame and easy to miss beside the larger AIA mark.

assets.issues: Good contrast, but the Nike swoosh is intrinsically small and subordinate to the shirt sponsor; it loses impact in anything wider than a head-and-torso shot.
assets.suggestions: Increase logo scale where kit regulations allow, or use higher-contrast outline/trim on the swoosh so it separates better in medium shots.

brands.name: Nike
brands.summary: Present on Tottenham kit, but visibility is limited by small mark size. It reads mainly in close-ups, not in standard broadcast wides.

examples.note: Visible on far-side LED in pregame wide, but distance makes the long copy hard to read quickly.
During goal celebration wides, long text competes with crowd and pitch action.

assets.issues: Copy length is the problem: even with decent contrast, a long promotional phrase is hard to parse in wide match cameras.
assets.suggestions: Shorten copy to a 2-3 word hook plus league bug, or split the message across sequential LED rotations with fewer words per exposure.

brands.name: 126 Live Premier League Games
brands.summary: The LED creative is serviceable but text-heavy. It is visible, yet not instantly digestible from standard broadcast wide angles.

examples.note: Far-side pregame LED is readable but still relatively small in the establishing wide.
In celebration/wide-play contexts the board is visible but partially competed away by player movement and crowd detail.

assets.issues: Solid short brand name and good contrast help, but perimeter placement keeps it secondary unless the camera lingers on the touchline side.
assets.suggestions: Use larger glyph height and more dead space around the logotype; avoid crowded companion copy so the mark pops in wide play shots.

brands.name: 12BET
brands.summary: A decent perimeter LED execution: short name, readable contrast, moderate visibility. Value is constrained mostly by distance and broadcast framing.

examples.note: Readable in pregame wide, but smaller letterforms and distance reduce snap recognition.
During fan/celebration cutaways the board is present but not focal, so legibility depends on viewer attention.

assets.issues: Longer wordmark than 12BET and less punchy contrast make it somewhat softer in wides.
assets.suggestions: Increase luminance contrast and consider a bolder, simplified wordmark treatment for LED use so letters hold at distance.

brands.name: Acronis
brands.summary: Visible on perimeter LED, but less forceful than shorter betting-style marks. Needs stronger contrast or simplified rendering for wide-shot effectiveness.

examples.note: Starting XI graphic is clear and dominant; no serious legibility issue.
Scorebug/goal-related Arsenal identifiers are small relative to full-screen action, so they function as identifiers more than branding.

assets.issues: Excellent in full-screen pregame graphics, but in scorebug usage the club branding becomes small and purely informational.
assets.suggestions: Keep crest/wordmark pairing larger in transitional graphics; for scorebug, slightly enlarge the crest or add more clearspace if branding value matters.

examples.note: Large stand bannering is visible, but the pan across the crowd means viewers get limited dwell time.

assets.issues: Strong club-color contrast, but signage is often captured in moving crowd pans rather than static branded holds.
assets.suggestions: Place larger Arsenal marks in camera-favored stand zones and avoid cluttered supporter-banner environments where multiple messages compete.

brands.name: Arsenal
brands.summary: Arsenal branding performs well in pregame graphics and stadium visuals. Club identifiers are clear, though some signage loses value because the camera treats it as atmosphere rather than a focal brand asset.

examples.note: If present on the pregame LED rotation, the long URL-style copy is difficult to read in one glance from the high wide.
During celebration/wide stadium shots, the slash-based copy structure becomes especially hard to parse at distance.

assets.issues: Longest and weakest-read message in the set: URL-style copy does not resolve quickly on far-side LED during live broadcast framing.
assets.suggestions: Do not run the full URL/message as a single distant LED read. Replace with a shorter CTA such as 'JOIN ARSENAL' and move the full web address to static close-range assets or digital overlays.

brands.name: Arsenal.com/membership
brands.summary: Low-efficiency creative for broadcast. The likely issue is not placement alone but the message format itself: URL-like copy is too long for perimeter LED readability in standard match cameras.
